newsitem.title: UK: Wheat prices rise on export hopes.
newsitem.headline: Wheat prices rise on export hopes.

text.p: Wheat prices in Chicago got an early boost on Tuesday from hopes of a pick-up in the export market but generally commodity markets had a slow day.

The key December wheat futures position on the Chicago Board of Trade gained six cents to $3.96 a bushel in early trade as traders got excited over news that Algeria was in the market for 150,000 tonnes and Pakistan for 270,000 tonnes of wheat.
Both countries included U.S. origin wheat in their tender specifications which raised hopes that U.S. exporters would win at least some of the business.
But some traders warned that U.S. wheat prices were uncompetitive with other world wheat producers which would harm export prospects.
On the London Metal Exchange (LME) tin prices tumbled to their lowest level for 1-1/2 years when the three months delivery position touched $5,760 a tonne, down $80 on the day.
Traders said investors continued to sell off their holdings against a background of recent sales of tin by China and Malaysia and generally poor sentiment in the base metals complex.
"Base metals in general are weakening and stop losses on longs have already been triggered on zinc and copper," said Elli Gifford of Investment Research of Cambridge in a daily report.
The gold market, which has seen wide swings over recent days in response to uncertainty in financial markets, quietened but still remained nervous.

It ended unchanged at $368.25 an ounce and analysts said the price is more likely to head lower than recover in the near term, with selling by mining houses seen capping rallies and slack seasonal demand failing to support prices. Among soft commodities coffee prices shot higher led by the New York futures where there was still concern over the level of stocks available to the market, despite the fact supplies from Latin American countries was starting to increase.
"Stocks are still really low, they are not at hundreds of thousands of bags which is where they need to be," a trader said.
New York December futures rose 2.50 cents to 108.10 cents a lb.
